I'm currently growing 4 different varieties of peppers and tomatoes in pots, is it smart to transplant them to a garden?

You should worry about root rot you don't want it to be wet while transplanting .Here a cool trick i learn back in the day . When it comes to plants with sensitive roots the best thing to do is to start them off in ice cream cones and then just plant the whole thing in the ground and the ice cream cone will rot away with time .

People use newspaper pots for the same reason. Take a rolling pin or thick dowel/post and wrap newspaper around it and fold it over the end of the dowel, stamping it down so it stays. They're flimsy without soil in them and can leak but they're great for disposable starter pots.

I grow most of my peppers and tomatoes in pots. They have better drainage than my soil, and I can control the nutrients better. I live in an area with a ton of hail in late spring/early summer, so pots also allow me to hide my garden in the garage when the weather goes to hell. I get better yields in pots as well
Make sure temperature outside is suitable, a cold frame helps between indoor and out door planting
